## Period {#fgt1-period .trig-lesson}

The **period** is the horizontal length of one complete repeating cycle.

```{=html}
<div data-trig="period" class="trig-demo"></div>
```

<p class="booklet-cue">Section 1.3 · A full cycle repeats the shape and direction.</p>

::: notes

This is a static comparison with no questions or reveal controls. Both sine curves, shaded full cycles, horizontal double-headed arrows and period rules are visible immediately. Define the fundamental period as the smallest positive horizontal shift that reproduces the whole graph. The arrows run from x=0 to x=2π for sin x and from x=0 to x=π for sin 2x; each covers a full cycle from one upward midline crossing to the next. Matching heights alone are not enough: the direction must also repeat. Periods are 2π and π. Connect the horizontal factor 1/2 to the halved period. Generalise to T=2π/|n| for sine and cosine, a,n nonzero; n is colour coded teal throughout. Tangent has T=π/|n| because tan x repeats every π; explain its construction later. Use radians throughout and keep the explanation brief.

:::
